---
title: Theming
description: The portal token contract, the four themes, and the self-hosted font registry.
---

A theme is operator-set: a palette, a default font, a corner preset and the brand mark. It is
mutable operator configuration, not form-grade immutable content. Respondent runtime choices, which
are mode, font and density, sit on top of the theme rather than replacing it.

QCMS is single-tenant, so one deployment runs one theme. Only the portal reads these values; admin
chrome is not adopter-themeable.

## Selecting a theme

| Variable                 | Values, default first                       | Effect                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_THEME`      | `slate`, `harbor`, `sand`, `plum`            | theme attribute              |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_CORNERS`    | `subtle`, `sharp`, `rounded`, `pill`         | corner preset                |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_MODE`       | `auto`, `light`, `dark`, `hc`                | default mode                 |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_DENSITY`    | `comfortable`, `compact`, `spacious`         | default density              |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_FONT`       | `system`, or a registry key                  | default font                 |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_FONTS`      | registry keys, comma or space separated      | the subset offered           |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_BRAND_NAME` | any text                                     | header mark and document title |
| `QCMS_PORTAL_BRAND_LOGO` | a root-relative path or a `data:` image URI  | optional logo beside the text |

An unrecognized value falls back to the default rather than throwing: a typo in presentation config
must not take a deployment down.

Mode, font and density are defaults, not settings. The respondent's own choice overrides them from
then on. Theme and corners have no respondent control.

## The four themes

| Key      | Name       | Character                                                     |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slate`  | Slate Teal | the shipped default: muted blue-green over cool slate neutrals |
| `harbor` | Harbor     | calm corporate blue; info shares the primary hue               |
| `sand`   | Sand       | warm neutral with a muted terracotta primary                   |
| `plum`   | Plum       | deep violet; info stays blue to remain distinct                |

Each is authored in light and dark, and each also declares a full light high-contrast palette and a
full dark high-contrast palette, every colour token in each, with body text at 7:1. Setting
`QCMS_PORTAL_MODE=hc` is how a deployment ships high contrast as its default.

Contrast targets are 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for UI in light and dark, and 7:1 for body text in
high contrast.

## The four token groups

Everything the portal renders resolves from a CSS custom property. There are exactly four groups.

| Group        | Tokens                                                                                               | Varies with                 |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| 1 Colour     | `--color-*`, 36 tokens                                                                                 | theme and mode              |
| 2 Typography | `--font-fallback-*`, `--font-portal`, `--font-mono`, `--type-*`                                        | the selected font           |
| 3 Spacing    | `--space-control-h`, `--space-control-pad-x`, `--space-field-gap`, `--space-section-pad`, `--space-stack` | density, three levels    |
| 4 Radius     | `--radius-control`, `--radius-card`, `--radius-sm`                                                     | the corner preset           |

Every rule is anchored on one selector:

```css
:is(:root, [data-qcms-theme-scope]);
```

The token set therefore applies to the document root, or to any element carrying the scope
attribute. An adopter's plain `:root` overrides work exactly as they would otherwise.

Corner presets are geometry only, so no contrast ratio depends on that group.

## Fonts

The family token is populated by a declarative, self-hosted font registry. The `woff2` files are
committed to the repository: a portal serves fonts from its own origin and makes no external
request for a typeface. There is no CDN and no build-time download.

| Group                    | Keys                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| System                   | `system`, always present and never removable                              |
| Accessibility            | `atkinson`, `lexend`, `opendyslexic`                                      |
| Popular                  | `inter`, `roboto`, `opensans`, `lato`, `poppins`, `montserrat`            |
| Playful and kids         | `andika`, `fredoka`, `baloo2`, `comicneue`, `patrickhand`                 |
| Traditional and corporate | `merriweather`, `lora`, `ptserif`, `librebaskerville`, `ibmplexserif`, `publicsans` |
| Monospace                | `jetbrainsmono`, `geistmono`                                              |

A respondent downloads one family, so the per-visit cost is small. `QCMS_PORTAL_FONTS` is the
curation surface: unset or empty offers the whole registry rather than an empty list, unknown keys
are dropped rather than fatal, and `system` is always offered and cannot be removed.

Every family is open-licensed and MIT-redistributable. The shipped subsets are Latin.

## Respondent controls

The header carries an Appearance disclosure with three controls: mode, font and density. Each writes
a cookie and swaps the root class immediately, with no round trip and no re-render of the form.
Without JavaScript the controls post a form instead.

## The brand mark

`QCMS_PORTAL_BRAND_NAME` is the text in the header and the document title. The name is always
rendered as text, and a configured logo sits beside it rather than replacing it, so the logo is
decorative and there is no alt-text variable to get wrong.

`QCMS_PORTAL_BRAND_LOGO` accepts only a root-relative path the deployment serves itself, or an
inline `data:` image, because the shipped content security policy allows only those two sources.

## Operating-system contrast

Two behaviours ship regardless of theming and need no configuration. The `prefers-contrast: more`
setting changes edges and focus rings only, inside the current palette. Under forced colours the
palette is the user's, and QCMS keeps shapes and states.

:::note
There is no admin theme editor and no per-form theming. Both are out of scope for this contract.
:::
